summary: Pre-alpha Python/FastAPI MES (v0.4.2, 15 stars, last push 2026-11-04) with substantial, test-heavy OEE, OPC UA and MCP code, but no Rust edge, Kafka, Temporal or Next.js; PackML and ISO 22400 are unimplemented or doc-only; the MCP tool count is 120 in code versus 95 in the README; and tenancy is per-database with no organization_id.

d1_oee.formula: OEE = availability x performance x quality. services/analysis.py oee_breakdown() sets overall = availability * performance * quality, or None if any factor is None. availability = running_seconds / observed_seconds from the coverage ledger (services/coverage.py availability()). performance = (cycle_seconds x units) / runtime_seconds via services/oee.py performance(). quality = good / (good + scrap). ISO 22400 is named only in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md ('ISO 22400-2 time model'); no 22400 citation appears in the code read.
d1_oee.storage: No persisted OEE column found in the files read. OEE is computed per request from equipment_states interval rows (domain/equipment.py EquipmentState), production counts (equipment_service.production_sums, production_logs table per migration b1f4c7a2e903), and the connection ledger (EquipmentConnection). Each request's result is returned, not stored.
gaps: Deliberately not clamped to [0,1]: services/oee.py docstring says 'a cap is a lie in the direction of flattery'. Performance above 1.0 is withheld (value None) with ratio kept and a named note (outruns_run_time).

Zero-denominator handling: performance None on no rating, not running, or nothing counted; availability None below min_observed_seconds; quality None when total is 0; overall None when any factor is None; coverage.withhold() blanks all factors below the coverage floor.
Docs list OEE/TEEP/FPY/MTBF/MTTR as the target KPI set (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md); only the OEE breakdown was verified in code.

d2_downtime.model: Open-interval state history. equipment_states rows carry started_at and ended_at; the open row (ended_at NULL) is the current state. The OPC agent (integrations/opc/agent.py) books intervals from the mapped State tag using the source timestamp. tag_map.py to_state() translates raw PLC codes via state_map, with '*' as an explicit catch-all; an unmapped value raises ValueError rather than being guessed. Downtime is state 'down', with optional reason text and reason_code from the plant's approved vocabulary (reason_map, reason_source recorded). Lost connection is a separate EquipmentConnection history treated as unknown time, not downtime (decision 0030). No PackML state machine.
gaps: PackML 17-state vocabulary is planned, not implemented: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md says 'machine states adopt the PackML 17-state vocabulary ... (M2)'. No PackML state names appear in domain/equipment.py.
planned_stop appears in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md but is absent from EquipmentStateName.
services/state_block.py defines STOPPED = {idle, down, setup, blocked, starved, disconnected}. blocked and starved are not in EquipmentStateName, and no code path read stores them.
No 'fault' state; the repo models faults as 'down' with reason codes. 'offline' is represented as connection state 'disconnected', not as a machine state.

protocols: OPC UA (asyncua client: data-change subscriptions on mapped tags, plus history and event subscriptions; writes via write_node)
MQTT (aiomqtt, optional [mqtt] extra; integrations/inbound/mqtt.py and integrations/uns/transport.py)
d3_device.edge_arch: No separate edge gateway and no Rust: the OPC UA agent (integrations/opc/agent.py, ~76 KB) is an asyncio Python process inside the fsmes package that reads tags and books state and counts into the plant database on the same node. The repo tree contains zero .rs files. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md describes a 'connect service' with driver plugins, which is not a separate service in the code.
d3_device.write_guard: write_node() in integrations/opc/agent.py calls shadow.guard(path) before node.write_value(), so shadow mode blocks it. write_approved_adjustments() writes only operator-approved recommendations whose tag is writable and within tag-map min/max bounds, and skips all writes in shadow mode. Tag map order_tag null marks a machine as read-only (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). _order_code_loop also writes order-code nodes through write_node.
gaps: Security default is anonymous and unencrypted: config.py sets opc_security='' and opc_user=''. Encryption is opt-in via MES_OPC_SECURITY (e.g. Basic256Sha256,SignAndEncrypt) with a self-minted client certificate that must be trusted on the server first (integrations/opc/security.py).
Order-code writes to the PLC are not gated by the approval queue; they rely on shadow mode and the order_tag mapping.
Shadow mode is the only runtime write gate; no write-rate limit or per-tag allowlist beyond manifest min/max bounds was found in the files read.

d4_data_model.hierarchy: ISA-95 equipment hierarchy in domain/masterdata.py: EquipmentLevel enterprise > site > area > work_center, with a free-depth tree below that (cell and machine, plus work units that carry tags and state history but are excluded from the OEE rollup). Materials, BomItem, Routing and RoutingOperation (with work_center_id) use ISA-95-style naming.
d4_data_model.shift_model: ShiftStamped mixin on state, log and audit rows: shift_code (String 40) and shift_day (date, the plant-local day the shift started). Intervals are stamped by the shift they begin in and are not split at boundaries; per-shift reporting clips to the window (domain/equipment.py comments; ADR 0028). Calendar and shift attribution come from migrations a1c5e83b7602 and c6a4b81f39d7.
d4_data_model.telemetry_schema: equipment_states (interval rows, indexed on equipment_id+started_at and ended_at); production_logs (counts, equipment_ts index per migration b1f4c7a2e903); tag_values with a latest-value index (migration e5f6a7b8c9d0); audit_log (ShiftStamped); outbox events in erp_messages. Timestamps are naive UTC (db.utcnow). UNS wire envelope is JSON with SCHEMA_VERSION 1 (integrations/uns/envelope.py).
d4_data_model.tenancy: Database per plant, not row-level. ADR docs/decisions/0021-one-database-per-plant.md measured 38 kernel tables with zero site, plant or tenant column; fleets are many databases with site identity. No organization_id column exists in the tree. Only hits for 'organi[sz]ation' are ADR 0009 (GitHub org) and tests/test_no_tenant_literals.py.

d5_api.versioning: No URL versioning. Routes are mounted per module without a version prefix: /auth, /admin, /ops, /masterdata, /workorders, /execution, /equipment, /dashboard, /assist, /documents (api/app.py include_router with Mount prefixes in modules.py). Package version 0.4.2 (README) appears in FastAPI metadata only.
d5_api.realtime: Polling, not push. The floor screen fetches one aggregate endpoint every 2 s (api/routers/dashboard.py comments; server-side caching about 1 s so the screen is never older than its own refresh). No SSE or WebSocket was found in the dashboard router. Not exhaustively checked across all routers.
d5_api.envelope: Outbox pattern: services/outbox.py records DomainEvents (equipment_state_changed, equipment_connection_changed, order_held, order_resumed) as erp_messages rows. The UNS wire envelope (integrations/uns/envelope.py) is JSON with schema_version 1, event_id = outbox row id, and plant always stated. Delivery is at-least-once; the file states exactly-once is not promised.
d5_api.auth: Passwords: PBKDF2-SHA256, 240,000 iterations (services/auth.py hash_password, hmac.compare_digest). Sessions: HMAC-signed tokens, accepted as Authorization Bearer or the mes_session cookie (api/deps.py). Only the system router (health and metrics) and /auth are public; all other routes require current_user, and write endpoints add role checks. Write idempotency keys in api/idempotency.py.

d6_ai.model: claude-sonnet-5 by default, overridable with MES_AGENT_MODEL (services/agent.py). The PRICES table also lists claude-opus-5 and claude-haiku-4-5. The benchmark's claude-sonnet-4-6 is not the default here.
gaps: README claims 95 MCP tools. Static count with the default MES_MODULES=all is 120 decorators: 36 in src/src/fsmes/mcp_server.py and 84 across 15 files under src/fsmes/mcp/. The 95 figure is not reproduced by the code read.

Tenant isolation is per plant database, selected by a 'plant' argument in each tool call. There is no organization_id or row-level tenant check; the benchmark's cross-org 404 rule does not apply here.
MCP HTTP transport sets allowed_origins=['*'] (mcp_server.py main); only allowed_hosts is restricted.
AGENT and ANALYST sign-in passwords fall back to plants.LAB_ONLY_* constants when FSMES_AGENT_PASSWORD or FSMES_ANALYST_PASSWORD is unset (mcp_server.py).

Rate limiting is per conversation, not per account or time window: MAX_ROUNDS = 12 model turns per person message, SESSION_TTL 30 min, RESULT_LIMIT 12000 characters, and a budget set in [admin] settings (services/agent.py). No requests-per-minute limiter was found in the files read.
Audit trail: audit_log table (domain/audit.py AuditLog, ShiftStamped) and an /audit endpoint with actor filtering (mcp_server.py audit tool). Append-only enforcement was not verified in code.

d7_quality.tests: 242 test_*.py files under tests/ (274 files including fixtures). Markers defined in pyproject.toml: slow, browser, erpnext_live. OEE-relevant tests include tests/test_equipment_oee.py, tests/test_kpi_budget.py, tests/test_ui_oee_above_rated.py; shadow-mode tests/test_shadow_mode.py; tests/test_no_tenant_literals.py. Coverage percentage was not measured.
d7_quality.ci: .github/workflows/ci.yml: test job runs ruff check and pytest on ubuntu-latest and windows-latest across Python 3.12 and 3.13; postgres job runs the suite and alembic upgrade head from empty on PostgreSQL 16.15 (image pinned by digest); browser tier (Playwright); wheel-demo; wheel-plant on Ubuntu and Windows; two-nodes-in-compose; two-nodes-on-windows; lab. Also dco.yml, scorecard.yml, release.yml and dependabot.yml.
d7_quality.migrations: 50 Alembic revisions shipped inside the package (src/fsmes/migrations/versions). Schema upgrades run under a PostgreSQL advisory lock (schema.py MIGRATION_LOCK_KEY). A database with no stamp is matched against revision shapes, not guessed. Every revision defines downgrade(); two are no-ops: 2c6e817b9faf (documented, PostgreSQL status columns stay text) and 153379d6cf19 (merge).
security_flags: OPC UA default is anonymous and unencrypted (config.py opc_security='', opc_user='')
LAB_ONLY fallback passwords for AGENT and ANALYST accounts when env vars are unset
System router (health and metrics) is public
No SAST or dependency-audit step (bandit, pip-audit, codeql) found in ci.yml; scorecard.yml and dependabot.yml do exist
d7_quality.last_active: 2026-11-04 (last push 2026-11-04T03:03:19Z; latest commit #222 'fsmes scenario'). 15 stars, 1 open issue.

adopt: Never cap OEE: withhold the figure and keep the ratio with a named note when counts outrun run time (services/oee.py). This conflicts with GreyHook's [0,1] clamp and needs an explicit decision.
Observed-time denominator and unknown-time ledger: time nobody watched is unknown, not downtime (decisions 0030 and 0033; services/coverage.py)
Coverage floor that withholds KPIs when the observed window is too short
Tag-map state translation that raises on unmapped values instead of guessing (integrations/opc/tag_map.py)
Outbox table with at-least-once events, event_id dedupe and plant identity stated in every envelope (services/outbox.py, integrations/uns/envelope.py)
Shadow-mode gate at the single write function (write_node calls shadow.guard)
Advisory-locked, in-package Alembic migrations on PostgreSQL
Idempotency keys on writes and dry_run on MCP write tools
Two-layer read-only analyst account (role plus plant-side refusal)
avoid: Per-database tenancy with no organization_id: conflicts with GreyHook's row-level organization_id and cross-org 404 requirement
A 120-tool MCP surface on one server with allowed_origins='*' and LAB_ONLY fallback passwords
Anonymous, unencrypted OPC UA as the default
README and docs claiming PackML and ISO 22400 before the code implements them
A README tool count (95) that does not match the code (120)
differentiate: Row-level multi-tenancy with organization_id on every row and cross-org 404; this repo has none
Rust outbound-only edge gateway with Kafka and Temporal workflows; absent here
A PackML 17-state model with per-driver mapping, which this repo plans but has not built
Claude claude-sonnet-4-6, read-only and rate-limited, with org-scoped tools; this repo defaults to claude-sonnet-5 with per-conversation round caps
Next.js 15 + TypeScript + shadcn/ui and ECharts frontend; this repo uses plain HTML/JS with no build step (ADR 0005)
